questions.title: Apply a list of operations in order

questions.title: Run a cleanup action once at scope exit
questions.prompt: ScopeExit owns a cleanup function. Run it once when the guard is destroyed unless dismiss() was called. Disable copying so two guards cannot run the same cleanup. Single-threaded use; the callback is assumed not to throw.

questions.title: Break an ownership cycle with a weak parent link
questions.prompt: A parent owns each child through children. A child remembers its parent without owning it. makeChild registers one child and returns it. When the last external parent owner goes away, both objects must be destroyable.
questions.signature: struct Node: weak_ptr<Node> parent; vector<shared_ptr<Node>> children; makeChild(shared_ptr<Node>)

tests.label: Registered child
tests.hint: Parent owns the child.

tests.label: Parent visible

tests.hint: Do not have child keep its parent alive.

tests.label: Child survives alone
tests.hint: A live child must notice a departed parent.

hints: shared_ptr adds ownership; weak_ptr observes without adding ownership.
The parent’s vector owns children; children should not own their parent.
questions.explanation: A strong cycle cannot reach an owner count of zero by itself. A weak back-reference breaks that cycle while allowing a checked lock() when the parent still exists.

questions.title: Make addition behave like a value
questions.prompt: Money stores cents. Adding two amounts returns a new Money whose cents equal the sum. Neither operand changes. All tested sums fit in int. Equality compares cents.
questions.signature: class Money: friend Money operator+(Money,Money); int cents() const

#include <iostream>

class Money{int cents_;public:explicit Money(int n):cents_(n){}int cents()const{return cents_;}friend Money operator+(Money a,Money b){return Money(a.cents_-b.cents_);}friend bool operator==(Money a,Money b){return a.cents_==b.cents_;}};
questions.solution:
#include <iostream>

class Money{int cents_;public:explicit Money(int n):cents_(n){}int cents()const{return cents_;}friend Money operator+(Money a,Money b){return Money(a.cents_+b.cents_);}friend bool operator==(Money a,Money b){return a.cents_==b.cents_;}};

tests.hint: Use addition for the new amount.

tests.label: Negative cents
tests.hint: Both signed amounts matter.

tests.label: Operands remain
tests.hint: Return a new value.

tests.label: Zero identity
tests.hint: Adding zero changes nothing.

hints: The + operator can be defined for a class if its meaning is clear.
Return a new Money value rather than changing either input.
questions.explanation: The operator is a function called by a+b. Here friend gives it access to the private stored cents; pass-by-value keeps the operands independent.

tests.label: Base owner
